summary: Shelby County, TX Texas Forest Service tower about 100 ft tall, described in a 1958 survey and staffed in 1946 and 1964; indexed as gone, with no site description found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure with a glass-enclosed cab, about 100 ft overall, colored gray
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association index marks it Tower Gone; no removal date or site description found

staffing.status: Forest Patrolman E. E. Covington reported from the tower in 1946; Texas Forest Service advertised a crewman position tied to it in 1964

events.note: Timpson Weekly Times (Aug 16, 1946): Forest Patrolman E. E. Covington of the Timpson forest fire lookout tower
July 1946 forest fire reported from the Timpson tower burned over 8 acres; Shelby County recorded 23 fires and 1,191 acres burned that year
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description (1958) gives the tower as about 100 ft overall, colored gray, about 6 miles SE of Timpson
Timpson Times help-wanted notice (Oct 30, 1964): Texas Forest Service crewman-equipment operator, living within 12 miles of the Timpson Lookout Tower, $100.00 per month

notes_for_editor: Brief height (30.5 m) matches the survey's about 100 ft, so no correction. The 1946 and 1964 items are newspaper clippings as reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; the story uses their wording, not the original papers, which we could not open. The 1946 report and 1964 notice both say Timpson, and the 1946 item names no fire date beyond July. Timpson Daily Times (1938) and Timpson Weekly Times (1944) pages on texashistory.unt.edu had no lookout mention. The Lufkin Daily News article returned 429 and the TFS history page 403, so neither was used. No build date, removal date or site description found. Two WebSearch calls. No photos added.
